title: Genetic Geometry: A Unified View of Genome-Wide Association Studies and LD Score Regression
content: Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) and LD Score regression are closely related in practice, yet the quantities used in these approaches have apparently different mathematical definitions. GWAS evaluates the association between a genetic variant and a phenotype, whereas the LD Score of a locus is defined from pairwise correlations among genetic variants. Here, we show that these apparently different quantities can be represented within a common geometric framework.We represent standardized genetic variants as vectors in the sample space and construct a symmetric positive semidefinite matrix from their outer products. Spectral decomposition of this matrix provides a common orthogonal eigenbasis for the genetic variation observed in the sample. Both individual genetic variants and the component of the phenotype contained in the SNP space can be represented using coordinates defined with respect to this same eigenbasis. LD Score and phenotype--genotype association can consequently be expressed as different operations on these common coordinates.We numerically verified these relationships using simulated genotype data containing correlated groups of loci and a phenotype vector constructed from components both within and orthogonal to the SNP space. Direct calculations of LD Score and phenotype--genotype association agreed with their corresponding spectral representations to numerical precision.These results show that GWAS association and LD Score are not quantities defined in unrelated mathematical spaces, but can be viewed as different operations performed within a common coordinate system.   We term this representation Genetic Geometry.  This framework provides a unified view of GWAS and LD Score regression and provides a basis for investigating why their locus-specific quantities exhibit the relationship exploited by LD Score regression.
